title: Review: Momentum and its conservation; Impulse and force–time graphs; Rotational kinematics; Torque; Moment of inertia; Moments and static equilibrium; Newton's second law for rotation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: R04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; R01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; R01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D08-1#N.5b, D09-ap2#N.10, D10-1#N.4b, R01-1#N.2, R02-1#N.5b, R03-1#N.11, R04-1#N.5b, D08-1#N.9, D10-1#N.12, R01-1#N.7, R02-1#N.2, R03-1#N.2. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Angular acceleration
items.clue: Symbol α: equal to the net turning effect on a body divided by its I.

items.label: Radian
items.clue: Unit of θ, defined by arc length over r; one revolution is 2π of them.

items.label: Angular displacement
items.clue: Symbol Δθ: how far a body has turned about an axis, final θ minus initial θ.

items.label: Crumple zone
items.clue: Car feature that lengthens the stopping time, making the average force smaller.

questions.stem: A uniform board of mass 3.0 kg and length 2.0 m rests horizontally on a pivot 0.60 m from its left end. What mass must be placed at the left end of the board for it to remain balanced?

An open cart of mass 3m rolls at speed v₀ along a level track with negligible friction. A ball of mass m falls vertically into the cart and stays in it; just before it lands, the ball's speed is 4v₀. What is the speed of the cart, with the ball in it, just after the ball lands?

Pucks A and B are at rest on level ice with negligible friction. Puck A has mass m, and puck B has mass 2m. Each puck is pushed by the same constant horizontal force F for the same time interval Δt. After the push, puck A has momentum of magnitude p_A. What is the magnitude of puck B's momentum after the push?
A disc on a fixed axle rotates 1.0 revolution counter-clockwise and then 0.25 revolution clockwise. Counter-clockwise is taken as positive. What is the disc's angular displacement?

A rod of length 0.60 m can rotate about an axle through one end. A string is attached to the rod 0.40 m from the axle and pulls on it with a force of 50 N directed at 37° to the rod. What is the magnitude of the torque exerted on the rod by the string's force about the axle? Use sin 37° = 0.60 and cos 37° = 0.80.

Two thin rods, X and Y, have the same mass and length. In rod X most of the mass is concentrated equally near the two ends; in rod Y most of the mass is concentrated near the middle. Each rod can rotate about an axis through its midpoint, perpendicular to the rod. Which claim about the rods' rotational inertias about these axes is correct?

options.text: Rod X's is greater, because more of its mass is far from the axis
Rod Y's is greater, because rod X's end masses give it more leverage
They are equal, because the rods have the same mass and length
It depends on where each rod is pushed, not on the rods alone

questions.stem: A solid disc of radius 0.50 m and rotational inertia 0.25 kg m² turns on a fixed axle. A string wrapped around its rim is pulled with a constant force of 2.0 N, tangent to the rim, in the sense in which the disc is turning. Friction at the axle exerts a constant torque of 0.25 N m that opposes the rotation. What is the magnitude of the disc's angular acceleration?

An electric fan is switched on, and after a few seconds its blades turn at a constant angular velocity. Which statement about the torques exerted on the blades while they turn at this constant angular velocity is correct?

options.text: The motor's torque is balanced by the opposing torques.
The motor's torque exceeds the torques that oppose the rotation.
The net torque is not zero, since each point on a blade accelerates.
No torques are exerted, since the blades are in equilibrium.

questions.stem: Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed

questions.stem: A light string is wrapped around a pulley of radius 0.0600 m that turns on a fixed axle. The string is pulled so that it unwinds without slipping while the pulley turns through 20.0 rad. What length of string unwinds from the pulley?
A wheel turns on a fixed axle through its centre. Four forces, each of 20 N and each in the plane of the wheel, act on it one at a time. Which force exerts no torque about the axle?

options.text: A force at the rim, at 45° to the spoke that joins that point to the centre.
A force halfway along a spoke, perpendicular to that spoke.
A force at the rim, pulling outward along the line of the spoke.
A force at the rim, along the tangent to the rim at that point.

questions.explanation: Its line of action passes through the axle (θ = 0°), so sin θ = 0 and the torque is zero, however large the force.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel can rotate about its axle. Which change would increase the wheel's rotational inertia about the axle?

options.text: Moving some of its mass from the rim in towards the hub
Spinning the wheel at a faster rate about the same axle
Pushing on the rim, rather than near the hub, to turn it
Moving some of its mass from the hub out to the rim
